prologue.heading: Not just how it looked. *How it felt.*
prologue.body: We watch for the split-second glance, the laugh nobody planned, the hand finding yours in a crowded room. Then we shape those fragments into photographs and films that still feel alive years later.
prologue.aside: A little direction when you need it. A lot of room to be yourselves.

items.summary: A riverside wedding full of yellow light, loud friends, quiet glances — and the kind of chaos that makes the best frames.
items.intro: A riverside wedding in Jim Corbett: a haldi drenched in yellow, a baraat under old trees, and a varmala beneath white flowers by the water. We stayed close enough to notice what mattered, and quiet enough not to interrupt it.

items.summary: A haldi in full colour, a sangeet under the lights, and a wedding night of petals and pyros.
items.intro: Three days of one family becoming two: a haldi that turned everyone yellow, a quiet afternoon by the pool, a sangeet under a sky of lights, and a wedding night of pyros, petals and a very long hug at the door. We kept close to the little things — a hem straightened, a hand reached for, a grandmother's arm.

process.heading: A calm process for a *wildly emotional* day.

steps.title: Meet, talk, listen
steps.body: We get to know the two of you and the shape of the day. No sales script — just context.

steps.title: Plan enough to breathe
steps.body: Timelines, family combinations, key moments and logistics are handled before the chaos begins.

steps.title: Be present, not intrusive
steps.body: We guide when it helps and blend in when it doesn't, so the photographs feel lived, not manufactured.

steps.title: Relive it properly
steps.body: Your gallery and films arrive as a body of work — not a folder of files you forget exists.
